_comment: Predefined interface categories: HOW an asset's access channel works.
Orthogonal to access-class (WHO may use it) and to operations (WHAT it exposes).
Each category declares its own fields; a field with "maps-to": "path" is stored
in the interface's existing path attribute rather than duplicated.
Free-form categories are tolerated — an id not listed here still loads.

categories.label: Device node (ioctl / read / write)
categories.description: A character device reached through a /dev node: open, then ioctl commands and/or read/write.

fields.name: dev-node
fields.label: Device node
fields.help: The path userspace opens. The runtime log matches interfaces by this.

threat-hints: command code validation and unknown-cmd handling
argument struct copy in/out, size and bounds
user-pointer TOCTOU between validation and use
file descriptor retained across a privilege change

categories.label: Mapped memory (mmap / dma-buf)
categories.description: A memory region mapped into an address space. Access needs no syscall, so nothing mediates individual reads and writes.
threat-hints: aliasing: two mappings of the same physical pages with different rights
use-after-revoke — the holder keeps the mapping after the owner frees it
page permissions weaker than the data's integrity requirement
no mediation per access once mapped

categories.label: Filesystem path
categories.description: A regular file or directory reached by path.
threat-hints: symlink and path-traversal races
permissions and umask
TOCTOU between stat and open
residual data after delete

categories.label: sysfs / procfs / configfs
categories.description: A kernel-exported text control or status file.
threat-hints: world-readable status leaking layout or keys
writable tunable that changes security posture
present only on debug builds

categories.label: Network socket
categories.description: A socket reachable over a network: remote parties can attempt to connect.
threat-hints: remote unauthenticated reachability
spoofing and replay on the wire
parser exposed to attacker-controlled bytes
resource exhaustion / DoS

categories.label: Local socket (unix domain)
categories.description: A socket on the local machine: peer credentials are available, file descriptors can be passed.
threat-hints: missing peer-credential check
file descriptor passing widens access
socket file permissions
any local process may connect

categories.label: Message passing (QNX / binder / D-Bus)
categories.description: A kernel-mediated message channel where each message is a separate authorization decision.
threat-hints: missing per-message authorization
connection id reuse or spoofing
unbounded message size or queue
confused deputy via a forwarded request

categories.label: Pipe / FIFO
categories.description: A byte stream between processes, named or anonymous.
threat-hints: no message framing — desynchronisation
writer identity unknown
blocking behaviour as a DoS lever

categories.label: Signal / event / fence
categories.description: Notification without payload: signals, eventfd, syncpoints, fences, interrupts.
threat-hints: forged or replayed notification
wait starvation and missed wakeups
notification used as a covert channel
ordering assumptions between signal and data

categories.label: Hypercall / VM exit
categories.description: A guest calling the hypervisor — the input crosses into a strictly higher privilege level.
threat-hints: guest-controlled arguments parsed at hypervisor privilege
shared ring buffer readable or writable by the guest after validation
one guest affecting another through shared state
hypercall available to an unprivileged guest process

categories.label: Secure monitor call (TrustZone / TEE)
categories.description: Normal world calling into the secure world.
threat-hints: non-secure pointer dereferenced in the secure world
shared buffer mutated after validation (double fetch)
secure world trusting a normal-world session id
denial of service against the secure monitor

categories.label: MMIO / register window
categories.description: CPU access to device registers through a physical address window. No OS mediates individual accesses.
threat-hints: register write reachable from userspace via a mapping
registers that reconfigure isolation (SMMU, firewall, clocks)
read of a register exposing keys or addresses
no bounds on the mapped window

categories.label: DMA / bus master
categories.description: A device reading or writing memory on its own initiative. The CPU is not in the path, so software permissions do not apply.
threat-hints: engine reaching memory outside its intended aperture
translation disabled, bypassed or misconfigured
descriptor or command buffer supplying attacker-chosen addresses
device access outliving the buffer's owner

categories.label: Kernel ABI (in-kernel call)
categories.description: A call between kernel components — no user/kernel boundary is crossed.
threat-hints: caller assumed trusted but reachable from a user path
no revalidation of data already validated elsewhere
callback registered by a less privileged component

categories.label: Debug / maintenance interface
categories.description: An interface intended for development: its presence in production is itself the finding.
threat-hints: shipped enabled by accident
full memory or register access
bypasses every other control
no audit trail

categories.label: Firmware / boot image
categories.description: A firmware image, boot partition or update channel. Authenticity and rollback matter more than access control.
threat-hints: unsigned or unverified image accepted
rollback to a vulnerable version
update channel writable by a lower-privileged component
verification performed after use

categories.label: Service API (HTTP / gRPC)
categories.description: A higher-level request/response API exposed by a service.
threat-hints: missing or weak authentication
authorization checked per route, not per object
input parsed before authorization
verbose errors leaking internals

categories.label: UART / serial
categories.description: A serial line. Physical access is the only prerequisite.
threat-hints: console shell reachable with physical access
no authentication on the line
bootloader prompt exposed
debug output leaking secrets

categories.label: USB
categories.description: A USB port or gadget interface: an attacker can attach an arbitrary device.
threat-hints: untrusted device enumerated automatically
driver parsing attacker-supplied descriptors
gadget exposing storage or network to the host
power/BadUSB class confusion

categories.label: PCIe
categories.description: A PCIe function. An endpoint is a bus master and can DMA unless translation constrains it.
threat-hints: endpoint DMA outside its aperture
config space writable by a guest
hot-plugged untrusted endpoint
ATS/IOMMU bypass

categories.label: I²C
categories.description: A shared two-wire bus: every device on it can see and drive the bus.
threat-hints: any device on the bus can impersonate another address
no authentication or integrity on the wire
EEPROM holding calibration or keys is writable
bus lock-up as a denial of service

categories.label: SPI
categories.description: A chip-select addressed bus, typically to flash or a sensor.
threat-hints: flash holding boot code is writable at runtime
no integrity on the transfer
physical probing of the lines
shared bus with a less trusted peripheral

categories.label: CAN / CAN-FD
categories.description: A broadcast vehicle bus with no built-in authentication.
threat-hints: any node can inject any message id
replay of recorded frames
bus flooding denial of service
no sender authentication
